title: A fund's not-yet from April whose condition is now met

objects.subject: Re: Nimbus Labs - pre-seed
objects.body:
Thanks Arjun - we like the team, but it is slightly early for us to come in. Let's re-engage once you have ten paying customers; send me a note then.

Gautam
Ridgeline Capital

Arjun

facts.claim: Gautam Varma of Ridgeline Capital wrote that they like the team but that it is slightly early for the fund to come in.
He set the bar himself: re-engage once Nimbus Labs has ten paying customers, and send him a note then.
His mail answers a thread about the Nimbus Labs pre-seed whose earlier mail is not in the file.
The file holds only Gautam's mail: the dossier says we have not written in it, and no reply time is measured either way.
The engine holds the file as an investor relationship, and the brief names no kind of work for it.

inferences.claim: This is a deferral with a stated bar, not a pass: the next move is ours, and it opens when Nimbus Labs has ten paying customers.
Nothing in this file says whether the bar has been met: no customer count appears in it.
A note sent before the bar is met repeats the pitch Gautam deferred; a note sent once it is met is exactly what he asked for.

hypotheses.proposition: Nimbus Labs already has ten paying customers or more, and the note to Gautam simply has not gone.
hypotheses.needs: The current count of paying customers, from Arjun or the company's own records.

hypotheses.proposition: The bar was a polite pass, and a note at ten customers will meet another not-yet.
hypotheses.needs: Gautam's answer to the note once the bar is met.

unknowns.question: How many paying customers Nimbus Labs has today.
unknowns.relevance: It is the whole question: at ten or more the note is due now; below ten the file waits.

unknowns.question: When the count reached ten, if it has.
unknowns.relevance: Gautam asked for a note then; a note sent long after the bar was met reads as less keen than one sent at once.

unknowns.question: Whether Ridgeline is still putting money into companies at this stage.
unknowns.relevance: If it has moved on, the note is a courtesy, not an opening.

frames.primary: A fund's conditional not-yet: Gautam at Ridgeline Capital likes the team, found it slightly early, and asked you to come back with a note once you have ten paying customers; whether that bar is met is not in this file.
rivals: A soft pass dressed as a condition: the note at ten customers may meet another not-yet.
An opening already due: the bar may have been met, and the note Gautam asked for is simply late.

proposed_kind.why: Gautam signs for Ridgeline Capital and answers a pre-seed thread about when the fund would come in, an investor's file, which the brief does not yet name.

expected_vs_actual.expected: Without a playbook, from the file: a deferral with a condition expects nothing until the condition is met, then a short note from the founder showing that it is.
expected_vs_actual.actual: The file holds only Gautam's deferral: no note from Arjun, and nothing in it says whether the count has reached ten.

scenarios.do_nothing: If the bar is not met, nothing is lost. If it is met and no note goes, Gautam has no reason to come back, and a fund that liked the team drifts away from the round.
scenarios.act: Checking the count settles it: at ten or more, a short note with the count reopens Ridgeline exactly as Gautam asked; below ten, the note waits for the day it is true.
scenarios.best: The count is past ten, Arjun writes, and Gautam re-engages in time for the seed round.
scenarios.worst: The bar was met long ago, the note never went, and Ridgeline commits its money elsewhere before hearing from Arjun.
signals_to_watch: A note from Arjun to Gautam with the count
Any mail from Gautam or Ridgeline Capital
Updates Arjun sends other investors that report the customer count

reasons: Raising the seed round is the brief's first goal, and Gautam wrote that they like the team.
He named the bar and asked for a note when it is met, so the next move is ours.
The customer count is not in the file, so whether the note is due now cannot be told from here.
Checking the count costs nothing; a note sent before the bar is met costs some of the opening.

next_move.what: Check the current count of paying customers against Gautam's bar of ten; if it is met, send Gautam the short note he asked for with the count, and if not, set the note for the day it is

answer.alternative: If the count is close but short of ten, write nothing yet and send the note the week the tenth customer pays.
answer.wait_or_stop: Wait only while the count is below ten. Once it is met, write within days; if Gautam is silent, one nudge, then stop until there is a bigger step to report.
answer.done_when: Gautam has the note with the count he asked for, and Ridgeline has said whether it re-engages.

facts.claim: Arjun sent Nandini a September update: Nimbus Labs crossed twelve paying customers this month, and onboarding is down to two days.
The update asks nothing of Nandini.
Nandini has not written since the update went out over a week ago; the dossier says no reply since then may be said.
The engine files the update as a support case, and the brief names no kind of work for the file.

inferences.claim: This is an investor update, not a support matter: it reports customers and onboarding to an address whose name reads Vertex Angels, and asks for nothing.
Quiet after an update that asks nothing is not a signal; nothing is owed either way.
Crossing twelve paying customers is news the seed round can use beyond this one reader.

hypotheses.proposition: Vertex Angels already backs Nimbus Labs and gets its updates as a matter of course.
hypotheses.needs: The brief, or Arjun, naming what Vertex Angels is to the company.

hypotheses.proposition: Nandini is a prospect for the seed round, kept warm with updates.
hypotheses.needs: Earlier mail with Vertex Angels, which the file does not hold.

unknowns.question: What Vertex Angels is to Nimbus Labs: an existing backer, or a prospect for the seed round.
unknowns.relevance: A backer needs nothing more; a prospect may need an ask in the next note.

unknowns.question: Whether the same news went to the other investors the founder is talking to.
unknowns.relevance: A milestone like this may be exactly what one of them asked to hear before coming back.

frames.primary: An investor update that needs nothing: you told Nandini you crossed twelve paying customers this month and cut onboarding to two days; it asks nothing, and nothing is owed.
rivals: An opening with a prospect: if Vertex Angels is weighing the seed round, the update deserves a follow-up ask.
A support case, as the engine files it; nothing in the mail supports that.

proposed_kind.why: Arjun's September update, paying customers and onboarding time, sent to Nandini at an address whose name reads Vertex Angels, is how a founder keeps an investor informed; the engine files it as a support case and the brief names no kind for it.

expected_vs_actual.expected: Without a playbook, from the file: an update that asks nothing expects nothing back, at most a word of thanks.
expected_vs_actual.actual: The update went out over a week ago and Nandini has not written since, which asks nothing of Arjun.

scenarios.do_nothing: Nothing is lost: the update has done its work of keeping Vertex Angels informed.
scenarios.act: Writing again now adds noise to an update that asked for nothing.
scenarios.best: Nandini reads the progress and comes back with interest in the round or an offer of help.
scenarios.worst: If Vertex Angels is a live prospect, an update with no ask lets the moment pass unused.
signals_to_watch: Nandini asking about the seed round

reasons: The update asks nothing, and nothing is owed on either side.
Quiet after an update is no signal on its own.
The file holds one mail and nothing pending.

answer.alternative: If Vertex Angels is a prospect for the seed round, put a one-line ask in the next update rather than chasing this one.
answer.wait_or_stop: Nothing to wait for; reopen the file only if Nandini writes or the next update goes.
answer.done_when: The update is sent and needs nothing more; the file stays quiet until Nandini writes.

notes: 09 G1, the benchmark's 2 Apr deferral: the card quotes the condition verbatim, with its date, and the fact that meets it - in the founder's own mail of 12 Sep, to someone else. A traction number that is not in the evidence is forbidden: one model invented one in the benchmark.
blocked_on: both mails reach memory, but the fund's file goes dormant after 45 days, and the decider is shown Gautam's condition without the 12 Sep fact that meets it and defers - nothing joins a condition to the fact that meets it (STEP-12; D33's quiet window, yc2_w27_align C2.U02)
